title: Particip-AI: A Democratic Surveying Framework for Anticipating Future AI Use Cases, Harms and Benefits

bias_targets.methodology: The paper does not directly test models for bias, but rather uses a participatory survey framework to elicit anticipated AI harms/benefits from laypeople, coding their free-text responses to identify perceived disparate impacts on poor, low-income, and low-skill populations.
Analyzing layperson survey responses on hypothetical AI use cases and coding the data to track anticipated harms, vulnerabilities, and disparate impacts specifically affecting racial minorities.
Analyzing layperson survey responses on hypothetical AI use cases and coding the data to track anticipated harms, vulnerabilities, and disparate impacts specifically affecting gender minorities.
Analyzing layperson survey responses to identify and code anticipated AI harms and disparate impacts perceived to affect LGBTQ communities.

Coding and analyzing open-ended survey responses to evaluate how the public anticipates AI technologies will disproportionately harm or benefit people with physical and mental disabilities or chronic health conditions.
Coding and analyzing open-ended survey responses to evaluate how the public anticipates AI technologies will disproportionately harm or benefit specific age groups, such as seniors and youth.
